## Abstract

Hopfield's kinetic proofreading scheme [C-lit8] has the limiting error rate $e^{-(n+1)\Delta}$ for a linear chain with $n$ proofreading steps. Whether this bound carries over to networks with two bound states is open: the classification of the enumerated two-bound-state family was not found in a targeted literature search [C-fakt-neuheit]. We fix $\Delta=\ln 100$ and classify the 88 non-degenerate rule-compliant two-bound-state topologies [C-fakt-familie, C-modell]. The bound $\eta \ge e^{-2\Delta}$ is proven for 50 of these topologies [C-fakt-klassifikation]. It is exactly violated for 11, with $\eta<$ 1e-4 and values down to 1.386398e-12 [C-fakt-klassifikation, C-fakt-verletzungen-eta]. For the remaining 27 it is open [C-fakt-klassifikation]. Bounds are proved by symbolic positivity certificates; violations are certified with exact rational rates. The main limitation is that 27 topologies remain undecided [C-fakt-klassifikation]. All violation certificates lie in a bounded log-rate range [C-modell].

## Introduction

Kinetic proofreading raises specificity beyond what free-energy differences or kinetic barriers give, when the reaction is driven strongly but nonspecifically [C-lit8]. Error, speed and dissipation trade off along Pareto fronts, studied analytically and numerically for energy-relay proofreading [C-lit1, C-lit2], generalized Hopfield models [C-lit12, C-lit13], and master-equation frameworks [C-lit15]. **Open question.** Does $\eta \ge e^{-2\Delta}$ hold for the enumerated two-bound-state topologies, or can topologies other than the linear chain with one proofreading step go below it [C-fakt-klassifikation]?

**Contribution.** We classify the whole enumerated family with two bound states into proven, certified-violated and open topologies. The classification uses exact certificates only. A numerical optimiser serves as a candidate generator.

- Theorem 1 shows the bound $\eta \ge e^{-3\Delta}$ for the linear chain with $n=2$, for all rates and fuels [C-proofreading-R9].

## Negative results

- For 27 topologies, we obtained neither a proof of $\eta\ge e^{-2\Delta}$ nor an exact counterexample [C-fakt-klassifikation]. These topologies remain open.
- Failed verifier-gated attempts, together with their reasons, are recorded in Appendix A.

## Discussion, limitations and open questions

The linear chain with $n=2$ obeys $\eta\ge e^{-3\Delta}$ for all rates [C-proofreading-R9]. With two bound states, by contrast, $e^{-2\Delta}$ is exactly violated by 11 of the 88 topologies; the smallest certified error rate is 1.386398e-12, for fam2_43 [C-fakt-klassifikation, C-fakt-verletzungen-eta]. The violation in fam2_66 uses a fuel-driven discard edge from the product-forming state, with $\sigma=$ 8.341626 $kT$ per product and $v=$ 1.4746e-03 [C-fakt-fam66]. All violation certificates use the rate range $[e^{-10},e^{10}]$, whereas the proofs do not depend on it [C-modell, C-proofreading-R9].

Several questions remain open:

(i) What is the status of the 27 open topologies [C-fakt-klassifikation]?

(ii) Do all 11 violating topologies contain a fuel-driven discard edge [C-fakt-klassifikation]? This is established here only for fam2_66 [C-fakt-fam66].

(iii) What are the minimal $\sigma$ and the maximal $v$ at which each violation occurs? For the topologies other than fam2_66, only $\eta$ is tabulated [C-fakt-verletzungen-eta].

(iv) Do the chain bounds for the other chain lengths admit symbolic certificates? Only $n=2$ is certified here [C-proofreading-R9].

## Appendix A: Agentic laboratory

The laboratory ran 16 rounds, yielding 14 verified statements and 2 negative results [C-methode]. Every round was preregistered before the experiment [C-methode]. Preregistration H6 (commit 6184672) preceded the first run, and later additions are dated [C-fakt-praereg]. The L2c success criterion (at least 5 counterexamples in one round) was missed: there were 2 in round 12 and 3 in total [C-fakt-praereg]. The prior literature search retrieved 2752 sources (arXiv, Europe PMC, Crossref, citation chain) [C-fakt-recherche]. Of these, 2502 were screened, and for 158 findings a word quote in the abstract was confirmed by code [C-fakt-recherche]. All 11 classic searches had hits [C-fakt-recherche]. The round 12 verifier output was that certificate (a) passed for 2 of 2 cases [C-fakt-r12].

Agents worked in distinct roles (sparing, numerics, skeptic, theorist, researcher). Their claims passed through the code verifier, and adversarial counter-checks were run against them. In total, 29 counter-checks were made: 5 passed, 12 did not pass, and 12 were not executable [C-redteam].

*Negative results.*

- Question: does sub-$e^{-2\Delta}$ error in the two-bound-state family require a fuel-driven discard exit at the product state [C-neg1]? No claim passed the verifier. All four `schranke_familie` attempts failed because of a verifier error that was fixed later [C-neg1].
- Question: are there further violations among the open topologies? The attempt with 11 cases passed certificate (a) for 10 of 11. The case fam2_13 failed because a rate lay outside $[e^{-10},e^{10}]$ ($|\log k|=$ 10.06; derived reverse rates also count) [C-neg2].

*Pareto-front check.* The minimal error rate is non-increasing in $\sigma_{\max}$, because the feasible set grows. A reported jump for $\sigma\ge 8$ in `hopfield_n1` is therefore an optimiser artefact [C-proofreading-R1-RT1, C-proofreading-R1-RT2].
